title: Indigo Verdict — AI Adoption Executive Briefing
description: Anchors every layout around a definitive before/after judgment — legacy vs. ML, on-prem vs. cloud — with oversized stat callouts underlined in vivid blue. A saturated gradient section banner and bilingual label support deliver the polished finish expected in C-suite AI readiness briefings.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment a tech lead must translate machine-learning complexity into boardroom-legible conclusions. It refuses process diagrams and step flows entirely — the executive audience has already decided to act and needs to see the delta, not the journey. Every layout gesture serves comparison and verdict: two columns, one number, one decision. The saturated purple-to-teal gradient banner signals premium authority without ornamentation; the thin gold rule is the only decorative flourish, and it earns its place by marking section hierarchy rather than filling space.
goodFor: Legacy-vs-ML technology comparison slides for non-technical executives
AI/ML adoption briefings anchored by a single dominant stat callout (e.g., '3.4× faster', '85% precision')
Bilingual Korean/English enterprise tech briefings requiring clean label hierarchy
Conclusion-driven board presentations where strategic direction is already set
avoidFor: Step-by-step process flows or onboarding diagram sequences
Consumer-facing pitches that require warmth, narrative arc, or emotional imagery
Dense multi-chart quarterly financial reviews with packed data tables
Creative portfolio or brand identity presentations requiring expressive layouts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a boardroom verdict being delivered — authoritative, restrained, and ceremonial. A cool, saturated gradient band commands the upper zone, projecting premium institutional weight rather than startup momentum. Below it, deliberate whitespace lets the title sit as a single unhurried declaration, uncluttered and final. Avoid photography, warm tones, or decorative layering; the only ornament permitted is the thin metallic rule that marks the threshold between the gradient identity header and the titling field.

examples.layoutNotes: The title slide opens with a full-bleed saturated gradient band bleeding edge-to-edge across the upper third of the canvas, carrying all header-identity weight. The deck title anchors in the left two-thirds of the remaining open field, separated from a subtitle or descriptor line by a single thin horizontal rule. A bilingual label pair (English dominant, Korean secondary) sits flush to the left outer margin at the foot of the slide, while a minimal deck identifier or date floats at bottom-right. No imagery, icons, or body copy compete with the title block; the gradient band and the rule line are the sole structural actors.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a boardroom verdict delivered in print — authoritative, compressed, and deliberately asymmetric in visual weight, with the dominant stat callout acting as the final word the eye lands on. The gradient banner at the top functions as a premium credential stamp, not decoration; everything below it is evidence supporting a conclusion that has already been reached. The two-column comparison carries controlled tension — left side reads as historical weight, right side as institutional momentum — with the accent underline on the stat punctuating the argument like a gavel strike. Avoid any visual language that implies process, journey, or exploration; this slide does not invite questions, it closes them.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with 6% outer margins; a full-bleed gradient banner spans the top ~18% of the slide and carries the section label with a hairline gold rule as its sole lower border. Below the banner, the body splits into two equal six-column panels — left panel carries the 'before/legacy' case, right the 'after/ML' case — separated by a single vertical rule. One oversized stat callout (the dominant verdict number) is anchored inside the right panel, underlined by a short vivid accent rule, occupying roughly the upper third of that column. Supporting label pairs (primary language + secondary language) sit flush-left inside their respective panels. Slide number appears bottom-right outside the grid margin; no footer band.
